<span id="a2399c88"></span>
# Event tracking planning

Before integrating the SDK, you need to perform event tracking planning based on your business analysis, and clarify what events and attributes may require event tracking in the business indicators to be analyzed. When planning event tracking, you need to understand some basic concepts and pre\-information such as event tracking events and properties preset by DataFinder, DataFinder's user identity logic, etc., and combine the capabilities provided by DataFinder to plan event tracking.

<span id="53f52e34"></span>
## Basic concept


|Basic concept |Concept note |Event tracking planning and SDK integration points |Detailed guidance document |
|---|---|---|---|
|Event, event properties, event public properties, user properties |DataFinder's user behavior data analytics is based on event + user model.<br><br><br>* Event & Event Attributes: A certain or a type of behavior of the user is called an "event". Event attributes are information such as the form and location of the event that are collected synchronously when the event is triggered to describe the event. For example, if a user purchases a product, then the user's behavior event is "Purchase", and the event attributes are "Product Name " , "Product Classification", "Payment Amount", etc .<br><br>* Event public attributes: Refers to **infrequently changing attributes** that are not strongly associated with an event and are common to multiple or all events, such as the version number of the application, device information, etc.<br><br>* User & User Attribute: User refers to the person who is the subject of the event behavior. User attributes refer to attributes of the user's own status (independent of behavior, such as age, gender, etc.) or user\-related attributes that are related to behavior but do not change frequently (such as VIP level, registration time, etc.). |You need to plan the events, event attributes, and user attributes to be collected according to the needs of business analysis. When integrating the SDK |See the detailed concept introduction [Data Model](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Data_Model). |
|Event tracking, full event tracking, custom event tracking |* Event tracking: Through the development of the SDK, the process of writing event logic into the code is called **event tracking** . DataFinder provides you with preset events and event properties, such events and event properties do not require you to manually event tracking, just turn on the capture switch .<br><br>* Full event tracking: is a kind of preset event and event properties provided by DataFinder. In DataFinder, the full event tracking events collected are bav2b_click button clicks and bav2b_page page browsing. No additional investment in research and development is required, but it will be at the expense of reporting a large amount of data, and only simple PV and UV can be collected, which is a bit'powerless' for the collection of rich business data.<br><br>* Code event tracking: Code event tracking refers to the development engineer who manually writes the code to implement the data collection logic according to the personalized needs of the business. Wide collection range and flexible application. However, it requires investment in research and development and requires certain technical capabilities. |It is usually recommended that you combine the preset events/properties provided by DataFinder with custom event tracking for event tracking planning. |[Event Tracking, Full Event Tracking](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Event_Tracking_Full_Event_Tracking) |

## Understanding data reporting requirements (format, quantity restrictions, etc.)

When planning for event tracking, you need to be clear about the data format requirements of the events and attributes to be collected and reported, as well as some restrictions on collection and reporting, so as to avoid subsequent failure to meet the requirements due to data formats, which will lead to data collection that cannot be warehoused and cannot be queried and analyzed later.

The data reported by the SDK usually has a fixed format, mainly including two parts: header and event.

## Understanding user identity logic

When planning for event tracking, you need to understand the user identity logic of DataFinder, which is used to combine the user identity logic of your own business to eventually unify the source of user identity data. DataFinder defaults to the **user** as the object of statistical analysis, and uses SSID as the user's unique identification ID to calculate the index. At this time, the user's SSID is the default statistical caliber. When your analysis object is a user, it is recommended to keep the default statistical caliber SSID. DataFinder can restore a real user individual through an SSID ID_Mapping after mapping the user's device_id, user_unique_id, etc.


* **device_id** : It can be used as the unique ID of the device, which is mostly used in scenarios where the user's real\-name ID cannot be obtained.

* **user_unique_id** : It is the login user ID, which is mostly used in the scenario where the user's real\-name ID can be obtained. Generally, the user ID used in the product business is directly used, such as the login account. When the user_unique_id is not set, in the SaaS version, the system will automatically use device_id replacement.

* **SSID** : for the DataFinder user statistics caliber ID, with the device identification device_id, login state user identification user_unique_id mutual Mapping, can ensure that the user anonymity and real\-name ID unified state.


See the mapping logic for the three types of IDs and more information about user identities [Supported User Unique Identifiers](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_User_Unique_Identifiers).

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">If there are multiple ID types for the user's real\-name ID in your business, for example, the user's real\-name information can be marked by multiple ID types such as account ID, user's mobile phone number, etc., you can also use the multi\-ID type function, see for details <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/undefined/6a4ce26a8f7714051e96f4c5">(不发布)Using Multi\-ID Types</a>.</div>



<span id="351948c9"></span>
## Understand the preset events and properties supported by the client side

As mentioned above, in most business analysis scenarios, you need to combine your own business characteristics for custom event tracking planning and integration. Before that, you can first understand the preset events and preset properties that the current DataFinder has provided you, and combine the existing preset events and attribute capabilities to further plan the requirements for custom code event tracking.


* See the list of app\-side supported preset events and properties [Android-Side Preset Events and Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android-Side_Preset_Events_and_Properties).

* At the same time, you also need to pay attention to the currently disabled preset attribute list. When planning custom event tracking and attributes in the future, you need to avoid the same name as the disabled attribute, otherwise the data will not be reported normally. See for details [Disable Properties List](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Disable_Properties_List).

# Preparation

<span id="f4224eb3"></span>
## Step 1 (optional): Create event tracking requirements/Enter custom event tracking

After completing the event tracking planning, it is recommended that you create the event tracking requirements according to the planning and then enter the custom event tracking into the DataFinder to complete the warehousing of the custom event tracking in the DataFinder metadata.


* Event tracking request management: You can manage event tracking requirements through DataFinder's event tracking request management function, and you can continue to maintain and manage requirements in the event tracking request management page to improve management efficiency. See the operation to create event tracking request management [Request Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Request_Management).

* Custom event tracking entry: You can first create custom event tracking metadata into the DataFinder according to the event tracking plan. For activity details, see [New event](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/General_Events#_2-1-%E6%96%B0%E5%A2%9E%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6), [Add event properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Event_Properties#_2-1-%E6%96%B0%E5%A2%9E%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6%E5%B1%9E%E6%80%A7), [Add user properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/User_Properties#533b53ea).


<span id="8c5ac3ed"></span>
## Step 2: Obtain the APPID/APP URL

Before SDK integration, you need to obtain the application ID (APPID or APP Url) generated by DataFinder when creating an application on DataFinder for subsequent SDK integration configuration.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">In the SaaS\-cloud native environment, the Android SDK has supported the security mode since the 6.17.4 version, that is, it also supports the use of APPID or APP Url for SDK integration configuration. You can refer to the following methods to obtain the application APPID or APP Url of the SDK to be integrated in advance. APP Url can be regarded as the encrypted APPID, and the configuration process is more secure.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">Other scenarios do not support the use of APP URLs for configuration for the time being. You can obtain and use the APPID for SDK integration configuration.</div>


* In the SaaS\-cloud native scenario, you can find the corresponding application in "Project Center" \> "Project Management" \> "Project Details", click "Access Data", and view the application ID (APPID) and APP URL of the application in the application details. For details, please refer to [Project Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Project_Management__).

When performing data access reporting, you need to confirm your data reporting address according to the current environment type and terminal type. If the reporting address is set incorrectly, you will not be able to report and query the data normally in the future.

### Reporting customs events

According to the event tracking plan, if you need to collect and report custom events, you can call the "AppLog.onEventV3" method to set the custom event name and event properties.


|Operation guidance |screenshot example |
|---|---|
|* Code event tracking that only reports events, as follows:<br><br><br>```Java```<br>```//Example: Report an event that does not contain properties```<br>```//placed in the corresponding position of business logic```<br>```AppLog.onEventV3("event");```<br><br><br><br>* Code event tracking for reporting events and corresponding properties, as follows:<br><br><br>```Java```<br>```//Example: Report an event, which contains two properties```<br>```//A property of type string, the property name is key_string, and the property value is value_string```<br>```//a property of type int, the property name key_int, the property value is 10```<br>```//placed in the corresponding position of business logic```<br>```JSONObject paramsObj = new JSONObject();```<br>```try {```<br>```    paramsObj.put("key_string", "value_string");```<br>```    paramsObj.put("key_int", 10);```<br>```} catch (JSONException e) {```<br>```    e.printStackTrace();```<br>```}```<br>```AppLog.onEventV3("event", paramsObj);```<br> |Without custom attributes:<br><br><span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/01b6d06ce46e43fa8a29b635402588dc~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span><br><br>With custom properties:<br><br><span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/13354e8299ee4b5398599c7d9686c7ba~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span> |



* Involving the core API:

   * onEventV3: Use the onEventV3 method to report custom events. This method supports a single event approach.


<span id="bb21600c"></span>
### Set up a custom user

If you need to set a custom user, you can call the AppLog.setUserUniqueID method to set user_unique_id property.

Usually, when a user needs to log in with a real name, the business will use an ID to uniquely identify the user. You can report the user ID of the corresponding business through the AppLog.setUserUniqueID method. Usually, this value can be obtained through the service interface, or an existing fixed user identification ID value can be directly read. The following fixed value is reported as an example.


|Operation guidance |Operation screen recording |
|---|---|
|* **user login**<br><br>   If there is an account system in your product, please set the uuid immediately after the user logs in to ensure the consistency of the caliber before and after the user logs in. 6.13.0 + version supports calling before initializing AppLog to set the uuid of the logged in user.<br><br>   ```Java```<br>```   //Set the ID of your account system and ensure its uniqueness```<br>```   //6.13.0 + version supports this method to be called before initializing AppLog```<br>```   AppLog.setUserUniqueID("your_USER_UNIQUE_ID");```<br>```   ```<br>   <br><br>   (6.13.0 + version is not recommended) Set the uuid through this method, and the setting will only take effect on the first cold start. Since AppLog.setUserUniqueID is supported before initialization in 6.13.0 +, it is no longer recommended to use this method to set uuid. It is recommended to use AppLog.setUserUniqueID uniformly.<br><br>   ```Java```<br>```   //set uuid during initialization```<br>```   //6.13.0 + version do not use this method```<br>```   config.setUserUniqueId("your_USER_UNIQUE_ID");```<br>```   ```<br>   <br><br>* **user logout**<br><br>   Called when the account is logged out.<br><br>   ```Java```<br>```   //Set uuid to null when logging out```<br>```   AppLog.setUserUniqueID(null);```<br>```   ```<br>    |User login:<br><br><span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/fb966e0c24464bee8b35bc8b18a79773~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span><br><br>user logout<br><br><span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/a88abb31943a47d48855c0c21abfcc44~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span> |



* Involving the core API:

   * You can use the AppLog.setUserUniqueID method to set the user's business identity ID \- user_unique_id, you need to understand the user identity logic of DataFinder before setting it up (see details [Supported User Unique Identifiers](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_User_Unique_Identifiers)), and see more introduction and parameter description of the AppLog interface.


<span id="d99c56a0"></span>
### Set up a reporting domain name

If your current environment is a SaaS\-cloud\-native or private environment, you need to set the data reporting domain name of the corresponding environment, that is, set config.setUriConfig during initialization. If the settings are incorrect, the data will not be able to be queried and analyzed normally.


|Operation guidance |Operation screen recording |
|---|---|
|```TypeScript```<br>```//First parameter APPID: reference, preparation - step 2 get```<br>```//The second parameter CHANNEL: fill in the channel information (which channel is your package currently uploaded to, such as Xiaomi, Huawei, Google), please note that it cannot be empty```<br>```//yourAPPID, yourCHANNEL as placeholders, please replace with actual content```<br>```final InitConfig config = new InitConfig("yourAPPID", "yourCHANNEL");```<br>```//Set the data upload address. You need to configure the upload address according to the region where the DataFinder service is used.```<br>```//Take volcanic clouds as an example here. For details, see the above, get the data upload address, part```<br>```config.setUriConfig(UriConfig.createByDomain("https://gator.volces.com", null));```<br>```//Make sure to start collecting user information before starting```<br>```config.setAutoStart(false);```<br>```//Full event tracking switch, true on, false off```<br>```config.setAutoTrackEnabled(true);```<br>```//true: open log, false: close log, closed by default, can be turned on during local debugging```<br>```config.setLogEnable(false);```<br>```//Encryption switch, true: on, false: off```<br>```AppLog.setEncryptAndCompress(true);```<br>```//Initialize once```<br>```//It is recommended to use this method for initialization in Applition```<br>```AppLog.init(this, config);```<br>```//It is recommended to use this method for initialization in Activity```<br>```AppLog.init(this, config, this);```<br>``````<br>```//Please call the following method after user authorization to start the actual collection of user information + reporting:```<br>```AppLog.start();```<br> |<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/f2e63bfcf97f44428ae3574cd5e6fd0e~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span> |



* Operation points: Before setting up a data reporting domain name, you need to clarify the environment and region you are using, and set the reporting domain name according to the actual situation. To confirm the type of environment you are currently using see: [SaaS Cloud-Native & Privatized Environments](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/SaaS_Cloud-Native_Privatized_Environments).

* Involving the core API: You can use the InitConfig interface to:

   * Set the reporting domain name by setting setUriConfig. Only SaaS\-cloud\-native and private environments need to be set.

   * If you also open the A/B experiment scenario, you also need to configure the offload address of the A/B experiment in the init interface according to the environment you use and the region you are located in.

<span id="46f2518e"></span>
## Event tracking data validation

After completing the initialization verification, you can perform the test operation on the client side to trigger some events to be collected and reported. After the test event is reported, within about 15 minutes, you can view the specific user behavior flow data on the `user scrutiny`page in the `growth analysis platform`, that is, you can see the test event and event attribute data, which is used to verify whether the event tracking data can be collected and reported normally.


* The user behavior stream data displayed in the user scrutiny page usually has a fixed format, mainly including `user`, `header`, `events`three parts, which respectively display the user attribute data collected and reported, public event attribute, event and event attribute data. The reported data contains preset and custom data that are opened for collection.

* If the corresponding event can be seen in the user's investigation, it indicates that the event was successfully reported. By observing the properties of the event, it can be confirmed whether the corresponding attribute was also successfully reported.

* If the data is not found in the user scrutiny normally, you can check it:

   * Whether the data format of the reported data meets the requirements: [Supported Data Formats and Event/Property Classification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification).

   * Check that the AppID in the integration code is correct [Import and initialize](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_Integration#eaa78476).

   * For SaaS\-cloud native and privatized environments, check whether the reported domain name in the integration code is configured correctly: [Set up a reporting domain name](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_Integration#d99c56a0).

# Android SDK API List

DataFinder provides you with a wealth of API interfaces. In addition to the core interfaces introduced in the above general process and the use examples of typical scenarios, you can also understand the main API interfaces currently supported by Android and their functions. According to business needs, you can flexibly call the corresponding interfaces to complete business tracking events.


|Classification |API List |API Description |
|---|---|---|
|main API |[init](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#b83be19a) |The SDK instance is initialized and configured, and the events generated after init are stored in the local database to ensure that the events are not lost. |
||[start](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#950f4bb1) |Launch the SDK, used with initConfig.setAutoStart, often for privacy compliance. |
||[onEventV3](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#43b682a2) |Report custom events, Android supports pre\-init/post\-init calls. |
||[setUserUniqueID](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#7fccc7c0) |Set user_unique_id, which can be called multiple times, and later settings will overwrite the same settings as before. |
||[setHeaderInfo](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#a608d39d) |Set the event public property, which can be called multiple times, and subsequent settings will override the same previous settings. |
||[removeHeaderInfo](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#73b75e64) |Removes event public properties. |
||[setEncryptAndCompress](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#c5906b8c) |Set whether the request is compressed and encrypted, which is enabled by default. |
||[getDid](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#33db8b05) |Gets the device_id of the current device. |
||[getSsid](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#2e94d9e9) |Get the SSID corresponding to the current user. |
||[addDataObserver / removeDataObserver](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#9bfc4a6c) |Add/remove all kinds of data callback monitoring, and use it together. |
||[setGPSLocation](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#d6b4a795) |Append GPS\-related custom properties to the event. |
|InitConfig API |[InitConfig SDK Configuration API Introduction](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#c73f46c7) |A series of configuration methods for InitConfig. |
|Module API |[AB test features and API introduction](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#a9dfd686) |The SDK provides AB experimental capabilities and provides a series of methods: getAbConfig, getAbSdkVersion, getAllAbTestConfigs, setExternalAbVersion, pullAbTestConfigs. |
||[User Attributes Module and API Introduction](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#9b071c87) |Provides the ability to set user properties and provides a series of methods: profileSet, profileSetOnce, profileUnset, profileIncrement, profileAppend. |
||[Element exposure function and API introduction](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android_SDK_API_Description#6590c90e) |Provides the ability to set exposure capture. |

## Console cloud control configuration

SaaS cloud native version or privatization V4.4.0 or above, DataFinder supports SDK settings through server level distribution, including reporting timing, full event tracking switch, etc. Please refer to the detailed introduction document: [Project Management - SDK Settings](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Project_Management_-_SDK_Settings).
